reviews.lens: REPRODUCTION AND NUMERICS: re-ran the proposers' decisive scripts and independent re-implementations, checked the replicas against the SPD07 BASE.json Rust counters, and audited JVP/flop accounting, error metrics, and fixed-trajectory vs closed-loop comparisons. All scratch files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vigilode/28b4ddd9-6979-5dcc-9dc3-5b21a0db99cc/scratchpad/algo/verify/repro_numerics/. I moved them out of verify/repro/ because another agent writes v_*.py files there.
reviews.general_issues:
1) How faithful the replica is (base_repro.py, base_small.log, base_160.log). mfrep.py 'base' matches SPD07 gmres_into_zero exactly on Bruss-50 and Bruss-160 at both rtols (attempts, accepted, rejected, jvp_vectors, linear_iterations: 30666/29200, 64561/61480, 56906/54800, 78255/74840), and exactly on vdp. Robertson is within 0.5%. HIRES is 6.7% / 7.7% high (78.6 vs 73.7 and 77.9 vs 72.4 JVP/acc): the replica builds 12689/48167 columns where Rust builds 11683/43841, because at n=8 the happy breakdown fires at a different point. Every HIRES ratio taken against the replica base is therefore about 7% too optimistic. The claim that the base 'reproduces SPD07 exactly' holds for the Brusselators and vdp only.
2) Fixed trajectories. probe_shared, probe_pc and probe_secant run on the dense-LU trajectory and do not feed stage failures back into the controller. That matters for Bruss-500, where base has 279 failed stage solves and shared has 32. probe_secant.py:118 and probe_pc.py:31 decide 'ok' from the recurrence (projected) residual, not the true residual. My reruns re-checked the true residual: the lag arms pass, the secant arm does not.
3) Costs left out of the JVP counts: the mu_D / Gershgorin bound needs J (n JVPs for small n, or 5 colored JVPs on the Brusselator, plus an eigensolve); orthogonalization flops; the secant SVD/Woodbury setup; banded preconditioner solves.
4) All replica JVPs are exact matvecs (W@v), and the SPD07 problems also use analytic user JVPs. The finite-difference JVP vulnerabilities raised in several candidates were never measured.
5) The PR-forced and quadratic-4 SPD07 cells are not in probs.py, so every prediction about them is unbacked by any replica run.
6) Error is measured the same way in every arm (NATIVE.json references, componentwise max relative), with the same h0 and controller. But equal rtol is not equal error on HIRES at 1e-8 (see KRY-PROJ-STOP).
7) The heat+upwind 'stagnation' family (n=64) is a GMRES(40) restart artifact. Restart 64 at the unchanged 1e-10 target removes every linear failure, at 276-398 JVP/acc.

verdicts.key_findings: Proj/base ratios reproduced with mfrep 'proj' and with an independent in-cycle Givens GMRES that continues the cycle and doubles the check gap (projstop.py, projstop_small.log, projstop_160.log). Bruss-50: 0.617 / 0.467 / 0.296 at 1e-3 / 1e-6 / 1e-8. Bruss-160: 0.731 / 0.618. Accepted/rejected sequences are identical, and final states differ from Rust by about 1e-11 normwise. probe_shared's 'full' arm gives 156.8/329.3 = 0.476. On every non-breakdown exit the true/projected residual ratio is 1.00 (exact matvecs), and the only failed checks are true residuals at cycle-end restarts, which base also pays. Small n: HIRES 0.712 / 0.557, Robertson 0.66-0.70, vdp 0.744-0.746, all against the replica base.
verdicts.corrections: (a) The claim 'neutral by construction / final error equal to base' fails on HIRES at 1e-8. At the unchanged 1e-10 L2 target the componentwise final error goes from 0.092 to 0.241 rtol (2.6x), and normwise from 0.044 to 0.241 (5.5x). Base's 4-5 decade overshoot was protecting HIRES's small components (atol 1e-12). Restoring base accuracy needs rtol_lin 1e-12: 47.1 JVP/acc, which is 0.60x the replica base and about 0.65x Rust (hires_err.log). Prediction (1) therefore fails on that cell. (b) Prediction (5), that n<=8 rows change only by the duplicate matvec, is false. HIRES columns drop 12689 -> 9703 at 1e-6 and 48167 -> 27524 at 1e-8; Robertson drops 1985 -> 1559 at 1e-8. (c) Against Rust rather than the replica base, HIRES is 0.76x / 0.60x. (d) Prediction (3), at most 1.2 checks per solve, fails if cycle-end residuals are counted: 1.38 on Bruss-50 at 1e-3 and 1.86 on Bruss-160 at 1e-6. Restate it as 'extra checks beyond restart residuals', which I measured at 0-1 per 736 solves. (e) The KILL rule 'true/projected > 10 on >1% of exits' would fire wrongly at n<=8. There, 5-88% of exits are happy-breakdown exits where the projected residual is about 0 and the true residual sits at roundoff, and all of them pass. Exclude breakdown exits. (f) The FD-JVP gap risk is untested.
verdicts.reproduced: Bruss-50 and Bruss-160 base reproduce Rust exactly; proj 174.8 / 101.0 (Bruss-50, 1e-6 / 1e-8) and 507.2 / 254.7 (Bruss-160) JVP/acc; Bruss-50 at 1e-3 0.617; full arm 156.8. Not reproduced: 'n<=8 change only by the duplicate matvec' and 'errors equal to base' on HIRES at 1e-8.

verdicts.key_findings: The certificate core reproduces. With exact mu_D there are 0 violations on accepted steps for Bruss-50, HIRES, vdp and Robertson at 1e-3 and 1e-6 (run8.log). Without the shift there are 34/115 and 119/351 on vdp and 1/41 and 2/204 on HIRES. There are also 0 violations in every heat+upwind arm. run16 reproduced: the Gershgorin bound costs +7% / +1% on Bruss-50, and the fallback rate is 30-60% on HIRES and Robertson. run11 reproduced exactly (1090->366, 1170->446, 1459->827, 1198->1065). Attribution test (stall_check.py/.log): the stall arm against certified forcing at the same theta, against letting the solve finish (maxit 2000), and against restart 64.
verdicts.corrections: Strike the stall-extension speed claims. Its own family refutes them. (a) The headline 1090->366 (0.34x) at a=60, rtol 1e-4, is entirely certified forcing: the stall arm equals the certified arm at 366. The stall increment over certified forcing at theta 0.02 is 1.00 / 1.08 (a=60, rtol 1e-4 / 1e-7), 0.80 / 1.04 (a=150) and 1.42 / 0.99 (a=300). At theta 0.001 it is 0.71 / 1.00 / 0.70 / 0.92 / 1.33 / 0.93. (b) Against 'let it finish' (certified, maxit 2000) the stall arm is 0.99-1.01x in 10 of 12 cells. At a=300, rtol 1e-4, it is 1.65x (theta 0.001) and 2.03x (theta 0.02) more expensive, with 9-12x larger error (0.183 / 0.240 vs 0.020 / 0.019). The cause is that a failed certificate rejects with err = 1+1e-9, so h shrinks by only 0.9. (c) The 'matched error 12.9k JVP at a=60, rtol 1e-7' figure is the certified arm without stall (586.3 x 22). The stall arm costs 13,976. (d) Restart 64 at the unchanged target dominates every arm: 276-398 JVP/acc, 0 failures. This family cannot show a benefit from stall acceptance. (e) The certification cost is understated because mu_hat needs J, which is never counted. Charging 5 colored JVPs per J on the Brusselator adds about 4-5%; charging n JVPs per J on small n adds about 15% on HIRES, 12% on Robertson and 6% on vdp, plus an O(n^3) eigensolve per attempt for the exact mu_D. Total certification overhead is therefore about +5-25%, not +0-10%.
verdicts.reproduced: Reproduced: zero violations with the exact shift; the unshifted violation counts; the Gershgorin percentages; the run11 table bit for bit. Not reproduced: any stall-attributable speed-up beyond 0.70-0.80x in isolated cells; the 12.9k stall figure.
verdicts.what_would_resolve: A genuine stagnation family with n >> restart, e.g. R-NEXT-03 CDR operators or 2-D upwind with n >= 1000. On it, compare stall-certified, let-it-finish (maxit 2000), larger restart and certified forcing at matched final error, with mu cost charged and with a stronger h cut on certificate rejection.

verdicts.key_findings: The fixed-trajectory probes reproduce exactly. probe_shared Bruss-50: 329.3 / 156.8 / 91.0 / 82.8. Bruss-160: 613.2 / 432.4 / 254.8 / 230.5. Bruss-500 (SKIPFULL): 1346.8 / 767.2 / 692.9 with failures 279 / 32 / 30 and peak dimension 980. Fischer 0.985 / 0.908 / 0.945. I also wrote a closed-loop replica (shared_closed.py): mfrep controller, stage RHS built from the shared inexact solves, true residual charged and re-checked. It gives Bruss-50 112.9 / 101.7 / 65.7 JVP/acc at 1e-3 / 1e-6 / 1e-8 and Bruss-160 289.7 / 171.7. Accepted/rejected counts are identical to base, |y - y_base| <= 7e-11, and no true-residual check fails. With retry: 89.0 / 92.4 / 64.9 and 262.0 / 170.2. Dot products per attempt are 7.6k on Bruss-50 (0.58x production) and 69k on Bruss-160 (2.8x production's 24.4k).
verdicts.corrections: (a) The space saturates near n on every Brusselator tested: peak dimension 100 / 318 / 980 for n = 100 / 320 / 1000. Per attempt the shared space (91 / 258 / 767 JVP) therefore roughly matches black-box dense assembly with J reused on retries (n x acc/att = 89 / 285 / 891 JVP/attempt), a saving of only 0% / 9% / 14%. Its orthogonalization (about 7.6k / 69k / 631k n-length dots per attempt) costs more flops than a dense LU (6.7e5 / 2.2e7 / 6.7e8). This comparator is missing from the evidence. (b) The small-n figures (HIRES 15, Robertson 10.8, VdP 10) are n+8 by construction and are beaten by dense assembly (8 / 3 / 2 JVPs plus a tiny LU). They should not be credited to this lever. (c) The right baseline is proj stop. Closed-loop shared/proj is 0.58 / 0.65 on Bruss-50 (1e-6 / 1e-8) and 0.57 / 0.67 on Bruss-160. (d) The Bruss-500 0.57x is a fixed-trajectory figure: base's 279 failures and shared's 32 failures (200-JVP budget) are never fed back. (e) With Brusselator-cost JVPs (~12n flops), the shared space at n=320 costs about 2.7x production in total flops. (f) The heat-200 and adv-diff gains come from constant-J problems: along y ~ phi, J = A + diag(3 nl (y-phi)^2) ~ A. These are best cases.
verdicts.reproduced: All JVP/attempt figures for Bruss-50/160/500 and the retry arm. In closed loop, the predictions Bruss-50 <= 115 (101.7) and Bruss-160 <= 310 (289.7) hold. Orthogonalization is 0.58x at n=100 and 2.8x at n=320, within the predicted 3.5x.

verdicts.key_findings: The JVP counts reproduce. probe_shared xstep: Bruss-50 35.6, Bruss-160 49.4 at k_max 400; probe_secant Bruss-160: 64.3 at k_max 320 and 49.6 at k_max 400, coverage 0.85 / 0.90; Bruss-500 at k_max 400: 586.6 with 127 failures. Re-checking with true residuals (secant_true.py): at Bruss-160, k_max 400 and the proposers' 1e-10 SVD truncation, 11 of 736 stage solves fail the true-residual certificate (true/threshold 1.1-5.4) while the recurrence residual reports convergence. The Woodbury capacitance K = I - h g Q^T P has cond 1.5e14 to 4.1e14. probe_shared's own xstep column already records 5 failures. Truncating at 1e-8 or 1e-6 removes every failure at 55.2 / 59.2 JVP per attempt (secant_tr8.log, secant_tr6.log).
verdicts.corrections: (a) The '0 failures' and 'no failures' claims in the coverage sweep rest on the recurrence residual (probe_secant.py:118). With the 1e-10 truncation, certified failures occur. Use truncation of 1e-8 or tighter, which turns Bruss-160 49.5 into 55-59 JVP per attempt (+11-19%). (b) Flops dominate, by a large margin. At Bruss-160 the SVD plus Woodbury setup costs about 2.9e8 flops per attempt, and the M applications another 2.2e7. That is about 14x a dense LU of W (2.2e7), or about 8e4 Brusselator-JVP equivalents. Against black-box dense assembly (n JVPs plus LU) the break-even JVP cost is about 1e6 flops per JVP. (c) The fair comparator was not run: a lagged dense J built from n JVPs per refresh and used as a preconditioner, i.e. PC-LAGGED-HWINDOW without structure. (d) Bruss-500 at k_max 400 has 127 failures vs 32 for shared alone, which confirms the stated partial-coverage harm.
verdicts.reproduced: Reproduced: 35.6, 49.4-49.6, 64.3, 586.6 with failures, and the coverage values. Not reproduced: 0 failures at full coverage under the true-residual check.

verdicts.key_findings: probe_pc and lag_only.py reproduce lag 57.9 / 62.4 / 62.6 and lagsh 42.2 / 46.1 / 46.4 JVP per attempt for N = 50 / 160 / 500, with LU per accepted step 0.183 / 0.159 / 0.159. All stage solves pass the true-residual check, so the N-independence holds. The lag arm needs 49-54 preconditioner (banded) solves per attempt; lagsh needs 33-38. The h-window identity W(h) = (1-rho)I + rho P, and the field-of-values containment for mu_2(J) <= 0, both check out algebraically. A refresh uses the exact J with h_P = h.
verdicts.corrections: (a) The relevant baseline is the existing banded direct driver, not production's 329 / 613 / 1347. Per sb_fast.json it costs 5 colored JVPs per J (82 J builds = accepted steps), 92 factorizations (1.122 LU per accepted step, not 1.0) and 8 solves per attempt. The lag arm costs 65-70 JVP per accepted step plus 49-54 banded solves per attempt plus 0.16-0.18 LU. On all three tested 1-D problems the direct driver is strictly cheaper, so no tested problem shows a winning regime. The 'high' expected value rests on 2-D/3-D fill-dominated problems that were never run, where P would no longer be an exact banded LU. (b) The adv-diff test has an effectively constant J along y ~ phi, the most favorable case for lagging. (c) Report the banded solves in total work, as the candidate's own probe asks.

reviews.label: repro:BC
reviews.lens: REPRODUCTION AND NUMERICS. I re-ran the decisive replica cells and wrote independent checks, which are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vigilode/28b4ddd9-6979-5dcc-9dc3-5b21a0db99cc/scratchpad/algo/verify/repro/ (v_*.py with matching .log files). I compared the replica baselines with the Rust counters in SPD07 BASE.json, in harness.md table 5.1 and in the r5_replica checks, and audited the replicas for counting, error and attribution bugs. I did not edit any proposer file and did not touch the worktree.
reviews.general_issues:
1) Baseline fidelity is good, with one exception.
- The dense replica (r5_replica.py and ctrl/rep.py, I controller) reproduces the Rust fast-driver counters exactly: vdP 1e-5 349/121, vdP 1e-7 654/95, HIRES 52/123/406. The vdP 1e-3 cell is 180/66 against Rust 181/67, as already documented.
- The matrix-free (MF) replicas reproduce the SPD07 gmres_into_zero arm: Bruss-160 1e-6 56,865 (kabort) and 57,152 (mfwp2) against 56,906, with attempts 92 in both. Bruss-50 1e-6 is 31,035 against 30,666. vdP 1e-6 is 15,008 against 14,996.
- HIRES is the exception: the MF replica overcounts JVPs by about 7% (76.9 against 71.6 per attempt), because of the n <= 8 full-space and final-residual accounting. This does not bias any controller ratio.
2) Every 'R-MF' baseline (31,392; 57,632; 66,101; 79,796) is the SPD07 zero-start arm, JVP + RHS. Production defaults to x0 = Previous (solver_types.rs, InitialGuess::Previous), whose counts are 3.8-6.5% higher on the Brusselators. The quoted ratios are therefore slightly conservative, not inflated.
3) The KRY replicas (kabort, kabort2, mfwp, mffail) advance the trajectory with exact LU solves and only simulate GMRES to count JVPs and decide failures. That is acceptable at linear rtol 1e-10, but they are counting replicas, not inexact-solve trajectories.
4) Many 'matched-accuracy' frontier numbers are linear-regression extrapolations outside the measured error range. Under the harness's own cheapest-run rule, the per-E ratios scatter by ±10-20% because of ladder granularity.
5) Two labelling or attribution bugs:
- In ctrl/dense2.py the 'enforce+max' column actually runs the single-solve own-W filter, because the test is mode == 'enforce'.
- kabort2's 'smart' docstring says q >= 0.98, but the code it imports (kabort.gmres) aborts at q >= 0.999.
6) Missing controls that changed conclusions:
- A uniform set-point arm (safety 0.725 on every step) reproduces most of the expansive-gate gain on vdP.
- An Enforce+max arm matches DENSE-OWNW's attempt savings exactly.
- Plain, non-extended projection reverses part of the KLEGAL narrative.

verdicts.key_findings:
The ROCK4 port checks out against OrdinaryDiffEq: the degree selection, the recf indexing (0-based offset is consistent), the embedded estimate, first-same-as-last reuse of the final f-evaluation, and counting the power-iteration f-evals. Counting is fair: nf includes the power iterations and the initial f0.

Runs:
- Bruss-50 (v_rock4_b50.log): ROCK4 at rtol 1e-6 uses 957 f-evals for error 1.63e-6, against the dense replica's 2.14e-6. At 1e-8 it uses 2,037 for 1.41e-8, against 2.16e-8. The ratios to the Rust zero arm are 0.030 and 0.031.
- Bruss-160 (v_rock4_b160*.log; reference ref160 agrees with my sparse Radau 1e-12 to 1.6e-11): 3,386 at 1.09e-6 needs ROCK4 rtol 1e-7, and 6,189 at 6.6e-9 needs rtol 1e-9. ROCK4's error is non-monotone in rtol: 4.6e-6 at 1e-6 but 6.0e-6 at 3e-7.
- Adv-diff n = 128 (v_adv.log): RODAS5P-MF base gives 26,501 ops / 14 linear failures / 5.89e-9 at rtol 1e-4, 31,693 / 27 / 2.73e-9 at 1e-6, and 23,148 / 0 / 5.09e-9 at 1e-8. ROCK4 at rtol 1e-9 gives 2,262 ops at 5.81e-9 with mean stage count 5.0, which is the minimum degree.
- Ritz angle for adv-diff is 1.84 (p7_ritz rerun).
- Fault injection (v_fault.log): reproduced. Final error is at most 6.2x rtol, cost is 2.6-12x, rejections are 20-24%.
verdicts.corrections:
1) The adv-diff 'gain' is not a stabilized-method gain. ROCK4 runs at its minimum degree (mean 5.0 stages, h·rho about 4-5), so it is effectively explicit RK4 against an over-resolved, solve-limited Krylov baseline whose error is independent of rtol (about 3-6e-9 at every rtol). The ratio range is 0.07-0.10, not 0.08-0.10. The written gate (angle <= 0.1) does not route this case (angle 1.84, confirmed).
2) ROCK4's estimator under-reports by about 5-15x at N >= 160. At equal rtol: N=160 gives err/rtol 4.6 (1e-6) and 15.6 (1e-8); N=200 gives 10.6-13.1 with exact rho. Matched-error ratios absorb this, but a deployed switch at the user's rtol returns errors 5-15x larger unless the rtol is tightened internally. The predictions should add an equal-rtol accuracy check.
3) Matched-error cells come from a coarse rtol ladder and ROCK4's error is non-monotone in rtol. Report the cheapest passing run, and accept that the 0.059x and 0.078x ratios carry about ±10% ladder granularity.
4) The baselines are the zero-start arm. The production default (Previous) is 3.8-6.5% more expensive, which slightly favours the claim; this is not an inflation.
5) The ratios against the improved RODAS5P arm (0.21x / 0.68x) are arithmetic from other candidates and were not reproduced here.
verdicts.reproduced: Reproduced: ROCK4 Bruss-50 957 @ 1.63e-6 and 2,037 @ 1.41e-8. Bruss-160 3,386 @ 1.09e-6 and 6,189 @ 6.6e-9. Adv-diff ROCK4 2,262 @ 5.81e-9. RODAS5P-MF adv-diff 26,501 / 31,693 / 23,148 ops with 14 / 27 / 0 failures. Ritz angle 1.84. Fault-injection table. Not reproduced (not run): Robertson, HIRES and vdP ROCK4 losses; the oscillatory RK-branch cells; the Chebyshev closure.

verdicts.key_findings:
rok.py's JVP charge (k = final basis dimension per step) is the minimal correct count. ROK4a coefficients match dl/rosenbrock_tableaus.jl:266-287, and btilde is used as the error-weight vector, which is the OrdinaryDiffEq convention (Rodas5P btilde = e_s).

Order tests (v_rok_order*.py, n = 12 nonlinear, nonstiff):
- Exact J: ROK4a order 3.99, RODAS5P order 5.05.
- Plain projection, M = 4 or 6 < n: ROK4a stays at order 3.98 (K-legal, confirmed), RODAS5P drops to 3.03 (K-order 3, confirmed).
- With the stage-RHS extension (extend=True, which every headline cell uses), ROK4a drops to order 3.01 at M = 4, 6 and 8, and recovers 3.98 only at M = n. As implemented, the U-form extension changes the projected operator between stages, so the measured '+ext' arm is not K-legal.

Bruss-50 rtol 1e-6 (v_rok.log): reproduced ROK4a M=16+ext 4,130 @ 1.48e-6, M=4+ext 2,454 @ 4.37e-6, and RODAS5P+ext 2.63e-5 / 2.94e-5 (silent). Plain-projection RODAS5P is not silent on Bruss-50: M=4 gives 5,268 ops at 9.44e-7 and M=16 gives 7,392 at 1.98e-6.

Matched accuracy with K-legal plain projection (v_rok_matched.log): ROK4a M=8 at rtol 5e-7 reaches 1.89e-6 with 3,300 ops, i.e. 0.105x R-MF and 0.63x the best matched RODAS5P-K run.

Bruss-160 (v_rok160.log): plain RODAS5P-K M=4 is silent (2.39e-5). M=8 is accurate (1.41e-6, 33,024 ops). ROK4a M=32+ext gives 7,088 @ 5.34e-6, as claimed.
verdicts.corrections:
1) 'Nonstiff order 4 holds for any M >= 4' is true only for plain projection. The '+ext' configuration behind every headline number is order 3 as implemented in rok.py.
2) 'The same projection silently breaks RODAS5P' holds for the extended projection on Bruss-50 and for plain M=4 on Bruss-160. It does not hold for plain projection on Bruss-50 (0.94-1.98e-6 at rtol 1e-6).
3) Restate the speed claim on the K-legal configuration: plain ROK4a M=8 reaches matched error at 3,300 ops (0.105x R-MF, 0.63x plain RODAS5P-K). This is better than the quoted 4,130 '+ext' figure.
4) The gated version and the complex-spectrum niche remain untested.

reviews.label: math:A
reviews.lens: Mathematical validity and prior art. I checked every identity and bound numerically or symbolically and rebuilt the tau constants from the fixture. Prior art was judged against the phase-1 literature maps plus standard references cited from memory, marked [MEM]. My scripts and logs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vigilode/28b4ddd9-6979-5dcc-9dc3-5b21a0db99cc/scratchpad/algo/verify/math_prior/. I did not modify any proposer file or the worktree.
reviews.general_issues:
1. The wrong theorem is cited for the matrix bound. The bound ||T_i(hJ)||_D <= sup_{Re z<=a}|T_i(z)| whenever mu_D(hJ) <= a in an inner-product norm is von Neumann's inequality for the half-plane, with constant 1 and no normality condition (Hairer-Wanner II, Sec. IV.11 [MEM]). Maximum modulus only explains why the sup sits on the line Re z = a. Crouzeix-Palencia's factor (1+sqrt2), which the raw INO text invokes 'otherwise', is not needed. Check: tau_vn.py, 300 random nonnormal 6x6 matrices in weighted norms, max ||T_i||_D/tau_i(a) = 0.99990. The proviso 'normal J' in INO-FORCE-ABS is superfluous. The real condition is mu_D <= a, and the Brusselator violates mu_D <= 0 on 91% of accepted steps.

2. The accuracy of the Krylov levers cannot be separated from target scaling. Production's L2-relative 1e-10*||b||_2 target looks adequate only because full GMRES cycles overshoot it by 4-5 decades. Any lever that stops at the target (PROJ-STOP, SHARED-SPACE, PC-*) exposes under-solving on small-component problems at tight tolerances. On HIRES, proj-stop alone raises the final error 3.4x, 5.1x and 30x at rtol 1e-8, 1e-9 and 1e-10 (projstop_hires.log). These levers need a WRMS or absolute target (INO-FORCE-ABS) before their 'neutral' accuracy claims hold.

3. JVP-only accounting hides flop costs. SHARED-SPACE acknowledges its dot-product growth. PC-SECANT does not cost its dense k x k LU and its O(nk) applications.

4. Several bound-validity checks are tautological. Zero violations on heat_pr and heat+upwind (linear, constant J, exact mu) are guaranteed by the theorem, so they say nothing about the nonlinear first-order claims.

5. The Python Krylov probes implement GCR (z = r or M r), not the GCRO/Arnoldi form the candidates specify. For the secant preconditioner I checked that this changes nothing: GCR and GCRO directions give identical failure counts.

6. Several proposer numbers depend on parameters that conflict with each other's calibration. CERT's stall speed-ups use theta = 0.02, which INO-FORCE-ABS deems unsafe.

verdicts.key_findings:
Mechanism. The Givens-updated |g_{k+1}| equals ||b - W x_k|| in exact arithmetic for unpreconditioned or right-preconditioned GMRES started from the cycle-start iterate. One true-residual confirmation keeps the certificate. This is textbook (Saad & Schultz 1986) and is standard in SUNDIALS SPGMR, PETSc KSPGMRES and scipy [MEM]; it is not a research mechanism, as the candidate admits. The beta/||r_true|| rescale under left preconditioning is only a heuristic trigger, which is safe because the true residual confirms.

Claim 'Neutral by construction' is false as an accuracy claim. It is only contract-neutral. projstop_tight.py (mfrep.integrate base vs proj, Radau reference at 1e-13):
- HIRES rtol 1e-8: err/tol 0.047 -> 0.158 (3.4x)
- HIRES rtol 1e-9: 0.044 -> 0.222 (5.1x)
- HIRES rtol 1e-10: 0.042 -> 1.252 (30x, out of tolerance)
- Step counts are identical (779/5, 1499/5).
- Robertson: 1.00x at 1e-8, 1.12x at 1e-10.
- The repro_numerics reviewer found the same independently: HIRES 1e-8, 0.092 -> 0.241.
Cause: the overshoot was masking an L2-relative target that is too loose for HIRES's small components (atol = 1e-4*rtol). This is exactly the inconsistency INO-FORCE-ABS describes.

Prediction (5) and the dropped item's reasoning are wrong. The claim is that n <= 8 rows change only by the removed duplicate matvec, and that the n <= 8 gain is almost entirely the duplicate final residual.
- HIRES 1e-8: 77.9 -> 43.4 JVP/acc, while the duplicate is only about 8.2/acc.
- Robertson 1e-6: 35.7 -> 24.3, duplicate about 8.4.
- In both, the projected residual reaches 1e-10*||b|| before n columns. That early exit is exactly where the error changes.
- Only van der Pol (n = 2) fits the duplicate-only story.

Overstated: 'no looser forcing can save a single column while cycles are full'. Multi-cycle solves (Bruss-160 at 1e-6, 77 JVP per stage, about 2 cycles) could drop whole cycles.

The FD-JVP caveat is correctly identified: the repo's two-arm addendum already had to relax GMRES to 1e-8 with FD JVPs.

Operative theorem: von Neumann's inequality in the D inner product. It requires only mu_D(hJ) <= 0; normality plays no role (the raw text's '(1+sqrt2) otherwise' is unnecessary).

The phi rule does not match its specification. The text uses the controller-predicted e_hat. verdicts.key_findings:
Identity. W(h) = (1 - rho)I + rho*P, hence W P^-1 = rho*I + (1 - rho)P^-1 for J_P = J. Verified symbolically with a sympy MatrixSymbol (fov_lag.py). The J-drift term h*g*||(J - J_P)P^-1|| is a correct field-of-values perturbation.

The field-of-values claims are correct but much weaker than what holds, and the 'Elman ~0.94, pessimistic' remark undersells the guarantee.
- If mu_2(J) <= 0, then Re<Py,y> >= ||y||^2, and Cauchy-Schwarz puts F(P^-1) inside the closed disc D(1/2, 1/2). Numerically max|w - 1/2| = 0.49998.
- Hence F(W P^-1) lies in D((1+rho)/2, |1-rho|/2).
- By the numerical-radius power inequality, ||r_k|| <= 2(|1-rho|/(1+rho))^k ||r_0||.
- That gives at most 22 GMRES iterations to 1e-10 for rho in [1/2, 2], and at most 47 for [1/4, 4], independent of h, N and stiffness for exact J.
- Elman's bound gives 158-714 iterations for the same cases.
- Three random nonnormal dissipative n = 300 tests needed 4-21 iterations and never violated the bound (max res_k/(2 rate^k) = 0.5).

The mu_2 > 0 caveat is real.
- F(P^-1) lies in D(1/(2c), 1/(2c)) with c = 1 - h_P*g*mu_2. For rho = 2 the guarantee requires c > 1/2.
- Brusselator (mu_2(J(y0)) = 6.97): h_P < 0.338. At h_P = 0.6, rho = 2, F(W P^-1) reaches Re = -0.17 and the guarantee is vacuous, though GMRES still took 15 iterations.
- So 'independent of h' holds only for mu_2 <= 0, or for h_P*g*mu_2 < 1/2 at rho <= 2.

Novelty is essentially relabeling of established practice:
- the CVODE/LSODPK lagged preconditioner with gamma-ratio refresh (lsetup/psetup when |gamma/gamma_p - 1| > 0.3, or every 20 steps [MEM]), i.e. a window of about [0.7, 1.3] vs the proposed [1/2, 2];
- Knoll & Keyes 2004;
- Birken et al. 2008, preconditioner freezing and updating in implicit time stepping [MEM];
- Blom et al. 2016, ROW with preconditioned Jacobian-free GMRES.
The disc bound does give a principled justification for the wider window. The trade against the existing banded direct driver is honestly stated.

reviews.general_issues:
1. Shift invariance is used by four candidates, and it holds much more narrowly than they assume. The four uses are KRY-BUDGET-PREDICT item 3 (retry h), CTRL-EXPANSIVE-GATE (Ritz form), REG-EXPLICIT-TRIAGE (Ritz angle and radius) and EXPRB-OWN-H (free phi1 actions).
   - K_m(I - h g J, b) = K_m(J, b) requires all of the following: no preconditioner, x0 = 0, the same right-hand side, and the first restart cycle only.
   - For stage 1 the right-hand side must also be collinear with f0. That holds for autonomous or autonomized problems only, because b1 = h g f0 + h^2 g gamma_1 f_t.
   - shift_proj2.log, unpreconditioned: the projected residual at h' equals true GMRES(h') to all digits (4.766e-2 vs 4.766e-2).
   - shift_proj2.log, with an h-independent diagonal or lagged-J right preconditioner: the naive projection is over-optimistic by 3 to 12 orders (4.8e-6 vs 4.5e-2; 5.6e-11 vs 7.8e-3; 4.4e-10 vs 8.5e-5; 5e-15 vs 9.6e-3). The Krylov spaces differ: minimum principal cosine 0.06-0.11.
   - Only a shift-and-invert preconditioner I - sigma J built with the current J keeps the space (cosine 1.0), and even then the projection coefficients differ.
   - Consequence: adopting PC-LAGGED-HWINDOW, or any h-independent preconditioner, silently voids all four uses.
2. Few of the "certificates" are rigorous. Three are rigorous within a stated scope:
   - DENSE-OWNW's ratio bounds, for normal J in the Euclidean norm with the same J;
   - the Jawecki defect integral in EXPRB-OWN-H, for mu(J) <= 0 with an exact Arnoldi relation and exact JVPs;
   - the CTRL-NULLS stage-growth bound, via Crouzeix-Palencia.
   The rest are heuristic or first-order: the q > 1 test in KRY-BUDGET-PREDICT needs a rounding and FD-JVP margin; the A ratio in GE-AMP-DETECT; rho1 in CTRL-EXPANSIVE-GATE; the "estimator-visible instability" argument in REG-EXPLICIT-TRIAGE; and the residual gate in KLEGAL-ROK4-GATED.
3. Several candidates are relabelings of known methods, which is fine provided they are presented that way:
   - CTRL-PRED-CAP is Hairer's RODAS/RADAU5 Gustafsson rule.
   - DENSE-OWNW Arm B is the Shampine-Baca/RADAU5 ESTRAD filter applied to the Rodas5Pr midpoint defect. Interpolating instead of landing is standard dense-output practice.
   - GE-AMP-DETECT is Lang-Verwer (SISC 29, 2007) first-variational-equation transport with tolerance-proportional re-run, plus a ratio.
   - The parts of REG-EXPLICIT-TRIAGE exist already:
     - Ritz-shape estimation from GMRES/Arnoldi for Chebyshev methods: Elman, Saad & Saylor, SISSC 7 (1986), available in PETSc as -ksp_chebyshev_hybrid.
     - Arnoldi dominant-eigenvalue estimation for stabilized explicit RK: SUNDIALS ARKODE LSRKStep SUNDomEigEstimator (https://sundials.readthedocs.io/en/latest/sundomeigest/SUNDomEigEst_links.html).
     - Ratio-and-hysteresis switching: LSODA.
4. Phase-1 facts I re-verified on the fixture (tab_checks.log):
   - K extra order-4 tree residual: -1.097e-3.
   - W conditions: order 2 holds; sum b alpha_ij alpha_j - 1/6 = -0.0436.
   - Y7 = Y6 + U6, Y8 = Y7 + U7 and y1 = Y8 + U8 hold to 50 digits.
   - R_i(-inf) = [1, -2.00, -0.93, 3.27, -1.006, 3.412, 1e-7, -2e-9].
   - 5 gamma = 1.0597.

verdicts.key_findings:
Item (3) identity is correct.
- W(h)V = V+Hbar gives J V = V+(Itilde - Hbar)/(h g).
- Hence W(rho h)V = V+((1-rho)Itilde + rho Hbar).
- shift_proj2.log: the projected residual equals true GMRES(h') at rho = 0.5 and 0.2 (4.766e-2 = 4.766e-2; 8.326e-3 = 8.326e-3).
- The replica (robust/kabort.py:66-77, proj_cols) correctly uses only the first cycle with x0 = 0. That is why it certifies only h' that converge within 40 unrestarted columns, which explains the ~3x conservatism.

The stated assumption 'or an h-independent preconditioner' is false.
- Any h-independent P other than cI, or a lagged-J P, breaks shift invariance.
- The naive projection is then over-optimistic by 3 to 12 orders (shift_proj2.log).
- Only P = I - sigma J with the current J keeps the space, and with different coefficients.

Item (2), the monotonicity certificate, is valid only in exact arithmetic, for an exactly linear operator, and with the true residual measured in the minimization norm.
- At the 1e-10 relative threshold, rounding at the attainable-accuracy floor (about eps * cond(W) * ||x||/||b||) and FD-JVP nonlinearity can produce q slightly above 1.
- So the test needs a margin, e.g. q > 1 + delta or q > 2. The L-0046 growth (6.5e-4 -> 6.4e13) is far beyond any such margin.
- It is a weaker special case of the standard residual-gap check (least-squares residual vs true residual), which also catches broken relations when q < 1.
- For GCRO-DR the invariant breaks whenever C is not recomputed as W_new U after W changes. Parks, de Sturler et al. (SISC 28, 2006) handle this explicitly.

Stagnation trigger.
- For deterministic restarted GMRES, q = 1 exactly implies permanent stagnation, because the next cycle repeats.
- q >= 0.98 is a heuristic. GMRES(m) plateaus followed by faster convergence are documented (Embree, SIAM Rev. 2003).

Parabolic cost claim is consistent with theory: iterations ~ sqrt(kappa) ~ h^(1/2), so JVPs per unit time ~ h^(-1/2). The predicted values 2.0/1.41/1.20/0.85 at h/h_acc 0.25/0.5/0.7/1.4 match the replica's 2.31/1.58/1.13/0.87.

- exp4 (Hochbruck, Lubich & Selhofer, SISC 19, 1998);
- phipm step adaptation (Niesen & Wright);
- shifted systems (Frommer & Glassner, SISC 19, 1998).

verdicts.key_findings:
Mathematics that holds:
- For W = (1+nu)I - nu S with S the nilpotent shift, W(S) is the disc of radius cos(pi/(n+1)).
- So W(W) is the disc centred at 1 + nu with radius nu cos(pi/(n+1)), which stays at distance >= 1 from 0.
- The disc FOV bound (constant 2) gives about (nu + 1/2) ln(2/eta) iterations, capped at n.
- Hence unrestarted Krylov cost per unit time is flat in h.
- With GMRES(40) restarts the cost is superlinear in h, so per unit time it rises with h. A small-h equilibrium is then not uneconomic in itself; only the wasted failed budgets are.

The speed claim fails mathematically on its own example.
- The routing rule sends advdiff(128, 0.01, 5) to the exponential branch (Ritz angle 1.84; merge note).
- The angle is right to do so: rock4_nn.log on that operator gives:
  - true eigenvalues real in [-1714, -244];
  - numerical eigenvalues already scatter to |Im| 379;
  - FOV Re [-1956, -1.3], |Im| <= 645;
  - power-method rho estimate 2138.
- ||R_ROCK4(hA)^k||_2 grows to:
  - 1.8e9 at h = 3e-3 (k = 179);
  - 5.5e37 at h = 1e-2;
  - 1e40-1e41 at h >= 3e-2.
  ROCK4 is not power-bounded there (Reddy-Trefethen).
- In trajectories (rock4_adv_run*.log) ROCK4 runs stability-limited at h ~ 2.3-2.8e-3 (h*rho about 6.5, median 6 stages), independent of rtol 1e-6 to 1e-9 (nf 2222/2203/2261/2262). It is held at the pseudospectral boundary by error-estimator rejections, not by an a-priori stability guarantee.
- I reproduced '2,262 at 5.8e-9' exactly, at rtol 1e-9 (5.81e-9). The number holds but is not reachable by the written rule.

verdicts.key_findings:
Closed loops verified symbolically (ctrl_loop.log):
- I controller: log e_{n+1} = c + Delta_n - eps_n.
- Gustafsson predictive (k1 = k2 = 1): log e_{n+1} = c + Delta_n - Delta_{n-1} + eps_{n-1} - 2 eps_n.
- theta = 0.9^5 = 0.5905; rejection when the phi ratio exceeds 1.6935.
- PI as coded has equilibrium 0.173 (matches rodas-core.md).
- Set-points match at theta for constant phi.

The proposed rule takes the min of the I and predictive steps, as Hairer does (lit-stab-ctrl: FACGUS ... max(QUOT, FACGUS)). So the realized loop is log e_{n+1} = c + Delta_n - max(0, Delta_{n-1}).
- It rejects iff Delta_n - max(0, Delta_{n-1}) > 0.527.
- It behaves like I whenever log phi was not growing on the previous step.
- 'Rejects only when the acceleration exceeds 0.53' describes only the case Delta_{n-1} > 0.

Noise: closed-loop noise variance gain is 5 (standard deviation x2.24) vs 1 for I. That is stronger than the per-step '2/k vs 1/k' sensitivity quoted.

Prior art: this is a relabeling of the textbook Hairer RODAS/RADAU5 PRED rule (Gustafsson 1994; Gustafsson, Lundh & Soderlind 1988). The RADAU5 source comment ('safer; classical often slightly faster for simple problems') is consistent with HIRES 1.06 at E = 1e-7. The work-precision regression protocol is standard benchmarking practice. The repo-level contribution is the adoption evidence, not the method.

verdicts.key_findings:
Arithmetic checks: (0.2/0.9^5)^(1/5) = 0.8053 and 0.9 * 0.8053 = 0.7248, whose fifth power is 0.2000. The R pole is at z = 1/gamma; all diagonal entries of beta equal gamma.

The merge correction is right.
- mu_2(J) <= 0 implies ||(I - h g J)^-1|| <= 1 at every h.
- The converse fails at finite h. Example: J = [[-a, k], [0, -a]] with k > 2a has mu_2 > 0, yet the resolvent norm is about k/(a^2 h g), which goes to 0 as h grows.
- rho1 is a single-direction lower bound on the resolvent norm. So rho1 > 1 implies mu_2(J) > 0, and it says nothing about the sign of Re lambda.

Empirical corroboration from the reproducibility reviewer's logs (verify/repro/v_gate.log, v_gate_uniform.log):
- On HIRES, which has no lambda_+ > 0, the gate still fires 237-238 times.
- On vdP it fires on 7060 of 9543 attempts (74%, GUS+gate) and 6480 of 9298 (I+gate). On vdP it is therefore close to a uniform safety change.
- A uniform safety reduction reaches similar fitted frontiers:
  - vdP I+uniform [137, 204, 305, 456, 680] vs I+gate [141, 205, 299, 436, 634];
  - GUS+uniform [125, 189, 285, 430, 649] vs GUS+gate [129, 189, 276, 404, 591];
  - Bruss-50: GUS+uniform is at or below GUS+gate at every E.
- The gate's increment over a uniform set-point is about 0-9%, and only at tight E.

The 'expansive-phase' rationale may also be confounded with 'fast-transition phase': any rapid change in the error constant causes I-controller rejections.

Prior art: log-norm-aware error propagation (Soderlind, BIT 46, 2006) and safety-factor tuning. The sign gate is moderately novel as a heuristic.

- Measured on the negative real axis: max 1.195765 at x = -4.7183.

The u'(1/2) = (y1 - y0 + (d1 + d2)/4)/h formula follows from the quartic interpolant.

- the same J in G and F (J_0 vs J_mid is not covered);

- Arm A: 0.945 (k <= 2), 0.78 (k <= 5), 0.57 (k <= 10), 0.35 (k <= 20).
- Arm B: 0.85, 0.52, 0.29, 0.15.

verdicts.key_findings:
res5 propagator. 5g = 1.0597, so (1 - g z)^-5 = exp(1.06 z) only to first order. Measured bias:
- per-step ratio (1 - g z)^-5 / e^z = 1.017 at z = 0.2, 1.062 at 0.5, 1.21 at 1, 2.13 at 2, 7.8 at 3 (pole at z = 4.72);
- on oscillatory modes it damps: |res5(i)| = 0.896, |res5(2i)| = 0.66, |res5(5i)| = 0.15.
So res5 over-amplifies exactly in the expansive phases it is meant to detect (false positives, e.g. part of the vdP 1e9-1e11) and under-propagates oscillatory amplification (false negatives).

The claim that 'A is invariant to the estimator's effectivity' is false except for a constant effectivity factor.
- Counterexample: 10 steps with gain 50 then 10 steps with gain 1 give a true A of 25.5.
- With effectivity 2 in the first window and 140 in the second (the 2-140x range the candidate itself reports), the estimate drops to 1.69 and the flag is lost.
- The proposers' own data show the underestimate: A_max 7.0/7.0/16.6 vs a true amplification ratio of 14.2/19.2/29.9, low by 1.8-2.7x.
- ctrl/amp.py:22-25 also divides a current-weight WRMS norm by a sum of per-step-weight norms, which adds further departure from invariance.

By the triangle inequality A <= max_k ||Phi(t, t_k)|| for fixed weights, up to res5 bias. So A is an estimate-weighted average gain and structurally prone to false negatives.

Prior art: the transport plus the 're-run with tolerance scaled by the transported estimate' response is Lang & Verwer, SISC 29(4):1460-1475 (2007): first variational equation with tolerance proportionality (they found it 'remarkably reliable' with ROS3P). Also Skeel 1986 and Cao & Petzold 2004. New elements: the res5 reuse and the ratio A.

verdicts.key_findings:
Cost-model constants verified:
- 4 sqrt(0.35 g) = 1.0894;
- 1.09 ln(2e10) = 25.8 and 1.09 ln(2e6) = 15.8;
- RK4 at |h w| = 2 sqrt 2 costs 4/2.828 = 1.414 rho per unit time;
- the Chebyshev-stage/ROCK4 ratio is about 3.27 asymptotically (4.6 at h rho = 10) for eta = 0.1, and 15.9 for eta = 1e-6.

'Chebyshev columns >= GMRES columns' is a theorem for any matrix (GMRES is optimal over the same Krylov space), not only for normal ones. The JVP-count closure is therefore rigorous, though Chebyshev saves orthogonalization flops.

The rho-independent sqrt(h_E/h_R) model presumes near-normal real spectra and accuracy-limited ROCK4 steps. It does not explain the adv-diff row.
- I reproduced 2262 f-evals at 5.81e-9 (rtol 1e-9).
- ROCK4 there is stability-limited at h of about 2.3e-3 (h * rho_est about 5-6.5, median 6 stages), with the same cost at rtol 1e-6 to 1e-9 (rock4_adv_run*.log).
- ||R(hA)^k|| grows to 1.8e9 at h = 3e-3 and to 1e37-1e41 at h >= 1e-2 (rock4_nn.log), so stability is held by estimator rejections.
- Power-method rho (2138) differs from the true spectral radius (1714) and from ||A||_2 (1956). FOV |Im| <= 645.
- The Ritz angle of 1.84 correctly flags that eigenvalue-based ROCK4 licensing is invalid there (Reddy-Trefethen). The merge correction should go further: admitting real-eigenvalue nonnormal operators is mathematically unsafe without a pseudospectral or FOV bound.

'Instability is estimator-visible' is empirical (the fault injection is fine), not a theorem.

Prior art contradicts 'no paper found using GMRES Hessenberg Ritz values for shape detection':
- Elman, Saad & Saylor, SISSC 7 (1986) hybrid GMRES/Arnoldi-to-Chebyshev ellipse fitting (PETSc -ksp_chebyshev_hybrid);
- SUNDIALS ARKODE LSRKStep SUNDomEigEstimator, with an Arnoldi module, for RKC/RKL stage selection (2025).
What remains new is using the implicit stage solver's own basis for family routing.

5. The Chebyshev-domination statement holds for all matrices in JVP count.

verdicts.key_findings:
Scale and shift invariance K_m(c h J, f0) = K_m(J, f0) = K_m(I - h g J, h g f0) is correct for nonzero scalars. The c nodes 1/4, 1/2, 9/10 and 1 match exponential.rs:907-914.

The zero-cost level-1 actions require:
- an unpreconditioned stage-1 GMRES with x0 = 0;
- an autonomous or autonomized problem, since otherwise b1 = h g f0 + h^2 g gamma_1 f_t is not collinear with f0;
- the first-cycle basis retained (the h = 0.3 case needs 41 columns > restart 40);
- no lagged or diagonal preconditioner. Under one, the basis is not K(J, f0): minimum principal cosine 0.06-0.11 in shift_proj2.log.

Count and fused-mode inconsistency:
- expo-cert.md:34 records 15 unfused and 5 fused augmented actions per step, vs the candidate's '4 of 7'.
- Fused actions use augmented starting vectors that mix f0 and D_i, so they do not lie in K(J, f0). The shared-basis saving and fused-action saving do not compose; the quoted '8.9k fused' cost cannot also take the free level-1 actions.

Certification:
- The Jawecki, Auzinger & Koch (BIT 60, 2020) defect-integral bound is rigorous for phi_p actions when W(J) is in C^- in the Arnoldi inner-product norm and the Arnoldi relation is exact.
- It certifies only the phi-action error, not the E step's local error, and not with FD-JVPs.
- The WRMS conversion factor 1/(sqrt(n) min w) is correct.
- The merge correction that mu_2 > 0 in the F-033 ramp window is consistent with GE-AMP-DETECT.

The repo records stiff order of about 4 (nominal 5(4); expo-cert.md:41).

Prior art: multi-scale phi actions from one basis are standard (KIOPS, Gaudreault, Rainwater & Tokman 2018; phipm, Niesen & Wright 2012); exponential vs implicit Krylov on nonnormal problems (Hochbruck, Lubich & Selhofer 1998; Loffeld & Tokman 2013). verdicts.key_findings:
What I confirm:
- The projected U-form solve u = V(I/(h g) - H)^-1 V^T r + h g (I - V V^T) r is correct.
- RODAS5P's extra order-4 K-tree residual is sum b G alpha^2 = -1.097e-3 (= 1/12 - sum b alpha alpha^2).
- Numerically (korder.log, n = 8 and 14, mpmath), local-error slopes are:
  - RODAS5P with exact J: 6;
  - RODAS5P with Krylov M = 4 or 5: slope tends to 4 (K-order 3);
  - ROK4a with exact J or Krylov M = 4 or 5: 5 (K-order 4).

The central claim fails in two ways.

(1) 'A K-legal tableau licenses a projected or reused operator' is false for reused operators.
- ROK4a with J + O(1) has slope 3 (W-order 2), the same as RODAS5P (slope 3).
- With a lagged J + hE both have slope 4.

(2) The measured contrast is not explained by K-legality.
- The measured contrast uses stage-RHS extension, which makes the projected operator stage-dependent in U-form.
- With that extension ROK4a loses its K-order (korder_n14.log, n = 14, M = 4): no extension gives slope 4.99 and error 9.0e-14 at h = 1/512; with extension slope 3.99 and error 8.6e-12. M = 5 and 6 give the same result.
- RODAS5P with extension is also order 3. Under the identical (extended) projection both tableaus are K-order 3.
- With pure projection, where ROK4a is genuinely K-legal, RODAS5P is not silently broken. Rerunning the proposers' rok.py (rok_ext.log, Bruss-50, rtol 1e-6) gives:
  - RODAS5P-K M = 4, no extension: 5268 ops, error 9.44e-7;
  - RODAS5P-K M = 16, no extension: 7392 ops, error 1.98e-6;
  - RODAS5P exact J: error 2.14e-6.
  Both are honest and 0.17-0.24x of RODAS5P-MF's 31,392 ops.
- The silent 2.6-2.9e-5 errors appear only with extension.

What survives:
- The Krylov-projected Rosenbrock idea itself, i.e. RODAS5P-K or ROK4a-K without extension. On Bruss-50 these give 3.5-7.4k ops at honest error.
- The recommendation of a true-residual gate.
Prior art: Tranquilli & Sandu SISC 36 (2014); Tranquilli, Glandon & Sandu JCAM 385 (2021), which itself leaves the effect of the extension unexplained.

reviews.general_issues:
1) THE ADMISSIBILITY PREMISE IS WRONG, AND THIS CHANGES VERDICTS. The repo does admit an arithmetic authority. SPEED_RESEARCH_STATUS.md:9-11 says: "The admissible unit is callgrind instructions per attempted step ... plus WorkCounters, counted operations and allocation counts". WorkCounters records orthogonalization_inner_products and orthogonalization_vector_updates (rodas5p-core/src/work.rs:32-33), and SPD07 BASE.json carries both: Bruss-50 at 1e-6 has 1,197,200 inner products, which is 13.0k per attempt. L-0084 gated only on linear matvecs, so a JVP-only gate has precedent. It is gameable, though. Every Krylov preregistration should therefore gate JVPs together with the orthogonalization counters or Ir, and should also gate preconditioner applications (banded solves).
- flops_shared.py re-counts the proposers' own fixed trajectories (common.trajectory). My base count is 13,495 dots per attempt, against 13,013 in BASE.json.
- On Bruss-50 at 1e-6, orthogonalization costs about 20x the JVP arithmetic (cost model: JVP = 8n, dot = axpy = 2n).
- KRY-PROJ-STOP: 0.47x the JVPs and 0.27x the flops of production.
- KRY-SHARED-SPACE: 0.58x the JVPs of proj-stop, but 2.8-3.1x its flops on Bruss-50 and 5.5-5.8x on Bruss-160.
- PC-SECANT-WOODBURY: 0.11-0.23x the JVPs of proj-stop, but 5.6-11x its flops.
- So the shared-space and secant gains are artefacts of counting JVPs only.

2) THE maxit=200 CONFOUND. Many robustness claims answer the same configuration artefact: raising maxit from 200 to 2000 removes most of the failures.
- stall_vs_big.py, heat + upwind n = 64, a = 60/150/300 at rtol 1e-4: 22/23/25 failures fall to 0, and JVPs fall from 33.8k/37.4k/40.7k to 10.8k/12.4k/13.6k.
- adv_big.py, autonomized adv-diff-128: failures fall from 14/27 to 2/0 at rtol 1e-4/1e-6.
- The failure counts of KRY-SHARED-SPACE and PC-LAGGED, the CERT stall arm, the SOLVE-LIMITED-SWITCH trigger and KRY-BUDGET-PREDICT are therefore not additive.

3) DOUBLE COUNTING. Several headline ratios against production already contain another lever's gain.
- KRY-SHARED-SPACE: its "unrestarted" column already contains proj-stop (157/329 = 0.48).
- PC-LAGGED (57.9 against 329) and PC-SECANT (0.108x) are measured on exact-stop GCR, so they include proj-stop too. Against proj-stop the ratios are 0.37x and 0.23x.
- KRY-PROJ-STOP's ratios include the duplicate final residual that was dropped as programming-level: 8 JVPs per attempt. On Bruss-50 that is 4.5% of the saving (0.479 against 0.467).
- CERT stall's 0.34-0.57x is made of three other gains: the raised budget, proj-stop, and forcing at theta = 0.02 (a theta that INO-FORCE-ABS itself rejects).

- adaptive.rs:264-306 implements only the Integral controller and the opt-in PI.
- adaptive.rs:396-446 has no post-rejection cap: an accepted factor is clamped to max_factor 5.
- F-078 is open (evidence.md A1).
- CTRL-PREDICTIVE is listed as contested only for lacking a matched-accuracy design (SPEED_RESEARCH_STATUS.md:66). It is not on the C list.

Prior art: it is the default controller of Hairer's RODAS, the L-0029 comparator with 1-14% rejections. So this is a port.

The proposers' own data show the cap is null:
- GUS to GUS + cap: 143/30 to 141/28.
- I to I + cap: 28.1% to 26.9%.
So the F-078 'closure' carries no measured benefit; the gain is the predictive term.

Matched accuracy.
- Its gate is a log-log regression frontier. That is a new rule, distinct from the harness rule (cheapest run with err <= E at {1e-3, 1e-5, 1e-7}; tools/stiff_benchmark_scipy.py:235-280). It must be preregistered and reported alongside the harness rule.
- CTRL-EXPANSIVE-GATE uses the harness rule, so the two candidates' gains cannot be stacked.

Defaults and interactions.
- It changes default results on every lane.
- Noise coupling: it requires absolute or tight stage targets, which positively couples it to INO-FORCE-ABS.
- It shrinks KRY-SHARED-SPACE's retry arm and KRY-BUDGET-PREDICT's failure memory.
- Evidence is the four stiff-benchmark problems plus Bruss-160 matrix-free (representative of the native benchmark). Corpus v2 appears only as a secondary prediction.

judged.combined_stack:
The levers are not independent multipliers. They compete for the same Krylov columns, the same failed solves and the same rejections, and two of them lose once cost is counted in admitted flops. Multiplying the headlines would give about 0.03-0.075x on Bruss-50; that is not realizable. Realistic combined effect against SPD07 BASE (zero start, linear rtol 1e-10), by problem class:

1) Matrix-free U-form, PDE-like real spectrum, no declared structure (Brusselator class), budgets not binding:
- The KRY-PROJ-STOP + INO-FORCE-ABS stack is measured (replica). Uncertified INO at theta 0.001 shows about the same increments as certified; the certified form is unavailable matrix-free.
  - Bruss-50: 0.40/0.35/0.27x JVP per accepted step at 1e-3/1e-6/1e-8 with theta 0.001; 0.34/0.32/0.25x at theta 0.002. Errors are unchanged on Bruss-50.
  - Bruss-160: 0.52x at 1e-6 and 0.54x at 1e-8 (theta 0.001).
- Orthogonalization falls faster than JVPs. Columns per stage go from 39.7 to 12.3 on Bruss-50 at 1e-6, i.e. about 0.1-0.15x the orthogonalization flops (proj alone: 0.27x).
- Adding CTRL-PRED-CAP is a further 0.90-0.96 (Bruss matched-error, matrix-free). Its interaction with INO's err_prev scaling is unmeasured.
- Realistic total: Bruss-50 about 0.30-0.33x JVP at 1e-6 and about 0.24-0.26x at 1e-8; Bruss-160 about 0.45-0.50x. In admitted Ir the Bruss-50 gain is larger, because orthogonalization dominates there.
- Not added, because they lose in flops or are not stackable: KRY-SHARED-SPACE, PC-SECANT and PC-LAGGED. Where a band is declared, PC-LAGGED is dominated by the SPD03 banded direct arm, which is the actual comparator.

2) Budget-failing cells (Bruss-160/300/500 at loose rtol; nonnormal advection):
- maxit 2000 with the stagnation guard is 0.76x at equal rtol on Bruss-160 at 1e-4, 0.42-0.55x at matched accuracy on Bruss-300, and 0.87x on adv-diff-128.
- It competes with INO, whose looser absolute targets also remove failures, and it absorbs the CERT stall (0.95-1.0x increment) and SOLVE-LIMITED-SWITCH (trigger becomes inert).
- The combination with proj+INO is unmeasured. Expect well short of the product, roughly 0.25-0.4x on Bruss-300 at 1e-4; this must be measured.

3) Small n (n <= 8) on the matrix-free path. This is not the production small-n path; the small direct driver serves it.
- proj-stop with a coupled target gives HIRES 0.59-0.73x (replica; about 7% less favourable vs Rust), Robertson 0.66-0.70x and vdP 0.75x. Net of the programming-level duplicate-residual fix, the vdP figure is about 1.0, Robertson 0.85-0.89 and HIRES 0.79/0.62.
- INO adds nothing here (0.92-1.16).
- PRED adds vdP 0.70-0.84 (much of it a set-point effect) and HIRES 0.85-1.06.
- Realistic totals: vdP about 0.55-0.62x, Robertson about 0.66-0.70x, HIRES about 0.55-0.70x, with error at most 1.5x base only if the stage target is outer-coupled.

4) Dense, banded and small direct drivers: only the controller applies.
- CTRL-PRED-CAP attempts at matched error: vdP 0.67-0.85 (largely reproducible by a uniform set-point of 0.725), HIRES 0.85-1.0, Bruss-50 0.90-1.0, Robertson 1.0. Rejections fall 4-5x.
- DENSE-OWNW applies only to opt-in Enforce dense-output runs: about 0.5x LU and Jacobian builds per sampled step at equal attempts. The attempt savings come from the max feed, which Enforce also gets.
- CTRL-EXPANSIVE-GATE overlaps PRED (at most 4-10% on vdP) and is not stacked.

5) Alternative families (REG ROCK4, EXPRB) are opt-in replacements, not multiplicative layers.
- ROCK4 is about 0.09-0.13x of the improved matrix-free arm on the Brusselator, but by estimate about 0.6x (N=50) to about 2x worse (N=160) than SPD03 banded direct when the band is declared.

- Neither is credited until its HOLD is resolved.

Accuracy caveat for the whole stack: proj-stop and INO change default results. On HIRES at 1e-8 to 1e-10 they need an outer-coupled WRMS or absolute target. The judge measured, at outer 1e-10:
- base 0.083 rtol;
- proj at any L2 target 1.9-3.0 rtol;
- proj with the absolute floor removed and rtol_lin 1e-12: 0.21;
- INO theta 0.001 uncertified 0.159, theta 0.002 0.60.

judged.cross_cutting_lessons:
1) Count admitted cost, not JVPs. The repo's admissible unit is callgrind Ir per attempt plus WorkCounters, which include the orthogonalization counters (SPEED_RESEARCH_STATUS.md:9-11; work.rs:32-33). A JVP-only metric can be gamed. Two candidates (KRY-SHARED-SPACE, PC-SECANT) flip from 0.1-0.6x to 2.8-11x once orthogonalization and setup are counted. PC-LAGGED omitted about 50 banded solves per attempt. CERT omitted the J needed for mu_hat. Every preregistration must gate JVPs together with orthogonalization counters or Ir, preconditioner solves and LUs.

2) Compare against the strongest cheap rival, not production.
- Krylov levers: proj-stop. Ratios against production double-count it.
- Failure-robustness levers: maxit 2000. maxit = 200 is a configuration artefact behind most failure counts.
- Declared-structure cases: the SPD03 banded direct arm. It probably beats ROCK4 at N >= 160 and beats PC-LAGGED on 1-D.
- Controller levers: a tuned uniform set-point.
- Dense output: Enforce + max feed.
- Synthetic stagnation families: restart >= n. The n = 64 heat+upwind family is not a stagnation test.

3) Removing overshoot exposes mis-scaled stage targets. Full GMRES cycles over-solved the L2-relative 1e-10 target by 4-5 decades, which hid that the target (and its absolute floor g*atol_lin) is too loose for small components at tight rtol.
- Judge checks on HIRES:
  - At 1e-8: proj gives 0.241 rtol vs base 0.092; 1e-11 or 1e-12 restores it.
  - At 1e-10: every L2-relative target from 1e-10 to 1e-14 gives 1.9-3.0 rtol vs base 0.083, because the absolute floor dominates.
  - The certified INO arm's relative fallback gives 3.78.
- Any early-exit or forcing lever therefore needs an outer-tolerance-coupled WRMS/absolute target, and matched-accuracy gates that include tight-rtol, badly scaled cells.

4) Attribute with control arms. Several headline gains belonged to something else:
- DENSE-OWNW's attempt savings come from the max feed.
- CTRL-EXPANSIVE-GATE's gain is a set-point effect (it fires on about 75% of vdP steps).
- CERT stall's gain is maxit + proj + theta 0.02.
- KRY-BUDGET-PREDICT's gain is the maxit change.
- SOLVE-LIMITED-SWITCH's gain is REG's ROCK4.
- KLEGAL's contrast comes from the U-form extension and projection size. Under plain projection, K-legal ROK4a is worse than RODAS5P at M = 4/8 on Bruss-160 (3.3e-4 / 1.3e-5 vs 2.4e-5 / 1.4e-6).

5) Fixed-trajectory and recurrence-residual probes overstate.
- With the 1e-10 truncation, the secant arm's recurrence residual hid 11 true-residual failures.
- Bruss-500 failures were never fed back into the controller.
- Closed-loop runs with true-residual certificates are mandatory before any robustness claim.

6) Krylov shift/scale invariance is fragile. K(I - h g J, b) = K(J, b) only when unpreconditioned, with x0 = 0, in the first cycle, and (for stage 1) on autonomous problems. Any h-independent or lagged preconditioner breaks it by 3-12 orders. So:
- PC-LAGGED excludes KRY-BUDGET-PREDICT's retry-h feature;
- it excludes EXPRB's free phi actions;
- it excludes the Ritz-based gates.

7) Theorem hygiene.
- The half-plane bound is von Neumann's inequality: constant 1, no normality needed, but it requires mu_D <= a. mu_D > 0 on 91% of Brusselator steps.
- 'Certified' should mean a first-order frozen-J bound unless the nonlinear remainder is bounded.
- Tabulated sup constants need inflation.
- Gershgorin bounds from FD entries are not rigorous.
- Linear constant-J zero-violation tests are tautological.

8) Matched accuracy is protocol-sensitive.
- The regression frontier and the harness cheapest-run rule differ by ±10-20% from ladder granularity.
- Several frontier points were extrapolated outside the measured error range.
- Preregister both rules, use multiple h0 seeds, and flag extrapolation.

9) Replica fidelity is uneven.
- The matrix-free replica is exact on the Brusselator and vdP, but 7% high on HIRES, so small-n ratios are about 7% optimistic.
- Every replica JVP was exact. The finite-difference-JVP risks named by several candidates were never measured.
- The PR-forced and quadratic-4 cells were never run.

10) The evidence base is narrow. It is Brusselator-dominated: real spectrum, mesh-independent RODAS steps, cheap JVPs. Corpus v2 families, 2-D/3-D grids, oscillatory and DAE cases are barely touched. That is exactly where the HOLD candidates' niches would have to live.

11) Most candidates relabel textbook methods: SPGMR in-cycle stop, CVODE eps_L, Hairer PRED, Lang-Verwer transport, ESTRAD, LSODPK lagged preconditioning, Elman-Saad-Saylor Ritz-Chebyshev, deflation preconditioners. Their contribution is repo-level adoption evidence under VigilODE's contracts, and they should be claimed and credited that way.

12) Explicit-branch stability on nonnormal operators is held up by the error estimator, not guaranteed: ROCK4's ||R^k|| reaches 1e9-1e41 on adv-diff-128. Any family switch onto explicit methods needs a field-of-values or pseudospectral step bound before admitting nonnormal operators.
